topic: Linear Algebra: From Geometry to Spaces

outline.topic: Linear Algebra: From Geometry to Spaces

sections.title: Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems
sections.content: Introduce a system of equations as the intersection of lines (in 2D) or planes (in 3D). Visualize the solution as the specific point where these geometric objects meet. Introduce the prerequisite concept: A matrix acts as a linear transformation.
sections.example: Imagine two robots (Line A and Line B) moving on a 2D plane. Their paths are defined by 2x + y = 5 and x - y = 1. The solution is the exact coordinate (2, 1) where the robots collide.

sections.title: Inverse Matrices: The 'Undo' Button
sections.content: Explain that if a matrix transforms space, the inverse matrix reverses that transformation. Use a visual 'stretch/rotate' animation to show how applying A then A-inverse returns the point to its origin.
sections.example: A 'Scale-o-matic' device doubles the size of a cat image. The inverse matrix is the 'Shrink-o-matic' that brings the cat back to its original dimensions.

sections.title: Column Space: Where Can We Go?
sections.content: Define Column Space as the span of the column vectors. Visually represent this as the 'territory' reachable by combining the column vectors. If the vectors are independent, they cover a plane/space; if dependent, they collapse into a line.
sections.example: A scout dog can jump in two directions (Vector 1: North-East, Vector 2: South-East). The column space is the entire flat field the dog can reach by combining these two jump patterns.

sections.title: Null Space: What Gets Crushed?
sections.content: Define Null Space as the set of all vectors that result in the zero vector when multiplied by A. Visually, this is the 'shadow' or the line/plane that gets squashed into a single point (the origin) during the transformation.
sections.example: A magical 'Flattening Lens' looks at a 3D forest. All trees standing exactly on a specific vertical line (the Null Space) are compressed into a single dot on the ground when viewed through the lens.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Connect the concepts: The existence of an inverse matrix implies the column space covers the entire output space and the null space contains only the zero vector (the 'no-crushing' condition).
sections.example: If our 'Flattening Lens' (Null Space) is empty, we can perfectly reconstruct the 3D forest from the 2D image using the Inverse Matrix.

storyboard.title: Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems
lecture_lines: Systems represent intersections of geometric objects.
Solutions are the specific meeting points.
Linear algebra links geometry and computation.
animations: Draw a 2D plane with lines #FF5733 (Line A) and #33FF57 (Line B).
Highlight the intersection point #FFFF33 where both lines cross.
Animate a vector #33A1FF moving from origin to intersection point.

storyboard.title: Inverse Matrices: The 'Undo' Button
lecture_lines: They act like undo buttons for space.
Applying A then inverse restores original points.
animations: Show matrix A #FFFFFF and vector x #FF5733 as input.
Display matrix A_inverse #33FF57 transforming result back to x.
Visualize the restoration process with a 'morphing' effect.

storyboard.title: Column Space: Where Can We Go?
lecture_lines: Column space is the reachable territory.
Independent vectors cover the full space.
Dependent vectors collapse space into lower dimensions.
animations: Draw two basis vectors #FF5733 and #33FF57 originating from center.
Fill the span of vectors with a shaded region #33A1FF.
Demonstrate adding a third vector falling within the span.

storyboard.title: Null Space: What Gets Crushed?
lecture_lines: Null space contains vectors squashed to zero.
It identifies what the transformation destroys.
animations: Show a transformation squashing space onto a line #FF5733.
Highlight the origin point #FFFF33 mapped to by the line.
Animate vectors along the null space collapsing to zero.

storyboard.title: Summary and Synthesis
lecture_lines: Inverses exist when space is preserved.
These concepts unify linear systems theory.
animations: Flash the four core concepts #FFFFFF in a grid layout.
Show them converging into a single unified formula #FFFF33.
Fade all elements out, leaving only the central formula.
